title: The Veil of the Weeping Wood
premise: Zephyrine Joubert, a hedge-mage mercenary whose god fell silent three years ago, survives by selling harmless charms in Vhalcrest, a city where magic is outlawed and the crown has begun hunting the gifted. When a former comrade arrives dying, carrying proof that Zephyrine's own soul was sold as collateral to the court beneath the mountain, he learns his silence-praying god never abandoned him—it was imprisoned, and its captors hold the deeds to every mage's soul. To reclaim himself, Zephyrine must assemble a crew of hunted outcasts, descend into the Weeping Wood, and bargain with the Pale Court; but the price they demand is that someone must take his place. In the end, Zephyrine shatters the ledger rather than trade another soul, freeing his god at the cost of his own magic—yet discovering that identity was never in the gift, and belonging was waiting for him all along among the people who chose to stay.
about_author: E. M. Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a small house at the edge of a forest that, they insist, hums at night.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He sells a luck-knot to a grieving fishwife in Vhalcrest's gray market, hiding the flicker of real magic beneath cheap tricks. Establishes his careful invisibility, his silent god, and the ache of a gift he cannot use. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Criers announce the Crown's Purge: all gifted persons must register or be taken. Zephyrine watches neighbors he's charmed for years look at him differently. He burns his ledgers and prepares to run. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under a life built on being unnoticed.

chapters.title: What Sera Carried Home
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. His old war-comrade Sera arrives at his door gut-wounded, clutching a black deed bearing his name and soul-price. She dies telling him the Pale Court beneath the mountain holds it—and that his god is their prisoner. Emotional beat: grief fused with terrible purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a flashback to the war. Reading Sera's stolen pages, he learns thousands of mages' souls were sold as war-collateral—including his own, signed by the commander he trusted. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing his whole past.

chapters.title: A Crew of the Hunted
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He recruits outcasts: Odile, a noble-born illusionist passing as human; Brannoc, a stone-singer who cannot lie; and Wren, a child pickpocket whose 'imaginary friend' is a minor spirit. Emotional beat: reluctant hope in found company.

chapters.title: The Road Through Ashfield
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew crosses a village burned in the first purge week, where survivors beg Odile to heal them and she must refuse to keep cover. Zephyrine quietly heals one child anyway, breaking his own rule. Emotional beat: the cost of caution versus conscience.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Register
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Crown witch-hunters with sniffer-hounds corner the crew in a river gorge. Brannoc collapses a cliff to save them, revealing his gift publicly and making him a marked man. Emotional beat: sacrifice as irreversible commitment.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Chapel
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering in an outlawed shrine, Wren's spirit-friend Ilex speaks aloud for the first time, warning that the Pale Court already knows Zephyrine comes. The group argues about turning back; none do. Emotional beat: fear shared becomes courage.

chapters.title: Where the Wood Weeps
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The crew enters the Weeping Wood, where trees bleed sap like tears and the dead whisper bargains. Zephyrine hears his god's voice for the first time in three years—a single word: hurry. Emotional beat: awe tangled with dread.

chapters.title: The Toll of Memory
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A wood-spirit demands payment in memories. Odile surrenders her sister's face; Brannoc gives up his mother's lullaby. Zephyrine refuses to pay and the forest marks him instead. Emotional beat: what survival costs when paid in pieces of self.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath Roots
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Guided by Ilex, they find the entrance to the Pale Court sealed by a riddle of names. Wren solves it using the alias Zephyrine gave her—the first name he ever chose freely. Emotional beat: identity as something given, not taken.

chapters.title: Court of Pale Lanterns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Descending into the cavern court, they are received with courtesy that curdles into menace. The Court's Steward shows Zephyrine his deed and offers him freedom—if another soul signs in his place. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Prisoner God
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Allowed one audience, Zephyrine finds his god chained in a lantern of bone: not mighty, but small and exhausted, having spent three years siphoning its strength to keep its faithful hidden. Emotional beat: shame and love colliding.

chapters.title: Bargains and Betrayals
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The Steward reveals a traitor among the crew sold information for safe passage. Suspicion fractures the group; Wren confesses she told a stranger about the door, not knowing what he was. Emotional beat: trust wounded but not broken.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The Court sets terms: bring them a soul of equal worth by the next moonrise, or the ledger activates and every registered mage dies. Zephyrine realizes the trap—they want him to become the thing he hates. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: What Odile Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals she once served the Court willingly, selling souls to buy her family's safety, and knows a back way into the vault. Her confession costs her the crew's ease but wins their plan its shape. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Theft of Souls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The heist through the vault of deeds: illusions, stone-song, and pickpocketing on a cosmic scale. Wren steals Zephyrine's deed—but alarms wake the Court. Emotional beat: triumph tipping into catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Steward's True Face
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered, they learn the Steward is the commander who sold them all, granted immortality as the Court's clerk. He offers Zephyrine his old life back if he hands over the crew. Emotional beat: rage meeting the man who made him.

chapters.title: Moonrise Over the Mountain
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax. Refusing every bargain, Zephyrine feeds his own deed into the god's bone-lantern, letting his god burn the ledger itself. The Court begins to crumble as ten thousand souls fly free. Emotional beat: self-destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Escaping the collapsing mountain, the crew carries a drained, mortal Zephyrine. His magic is gone; his god, freed, whispers thanks and departs into the world. Emotional beat: hollow victory, tenderly held.

chapters.title: Small Charms Still
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Months later, in a rebuilt Vhalcrest where magic is merely legal again, Zephyrine sells charms that are only charms—and finds he no longer minds. Wren visits; Odile writes; Brannoc sings. Emotional beat: peace without power.

chapters.title: The Veil Lifted
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, closing. At Sera's grave, Zephyrine plants a cutting from the Weeping Wood. It does not weep; it blooms. He finally understands survival was never the price—forgetting who you are was. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
